# `sesam config reset` rewrites sesam.yml to describe the audit log again,
# throwing away whatever the file declared on top of it. It is the opposite of
# `sesam config apply` and never touches the log. Without --force it only
# reports what it would do and leaves every file exactly as it is; --force is
# what actually writes it.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Nothing to do when the two already agree - silent, like git diff, with or
# without --force.
exec sesam config reset
! stdout .
exec sesam config reset --force
! stdout .

# Hand edits: a normal run only reports what would be discarded, and writes
# nothing.
cp edited.yml sesam.yml
envsubst sesam.yml
! exec sesam config diff
stdout '\+  - name: carol'

exec sesam config reset
! stdout .
stderr 'would discard'
stderr 'pass --force'

# Still there - nothing was written.
! exec sesam config diff
stdout '\+  - name: carol'

# --force is what actually writes it.
exec sesam config reset --force
! stdout .
stderr 'discarded'
exec sesam config diff
! stdout .

# The audit log is untouched by all of this.
exec sesam user list
stdout 'bob'
! stdout 'carol'
exec sesam verify

# A config too broken to read can only be replaced wholesale, which costs its
# comments - a normal run warns about that instead of failing, and still
# writes nothing.
cp broken.yml sesam.yml
exec sesam config reset
! stdout .
stderr 'cannot be repaired in place'
stderr 'would write it fresh'
stderr 'pass --force'
grep 'valid yaml at all' sesam.yml

exec sesam config reset --force
! stdout .
stderr 'cannot be repaired in place'
stderr 'wrote it fresh'
stderr 'comments and descriptions are gone'

# What it wrote describes the log exactly, so apply has nothing to do.
exec sesam config diff
! stdout .
exec sesam apply
! stdout .
exec sesam verify

# Even a deleted sesam.yml is recoverable - with --force, since there is
# nothing to repair in place.
rm sesam.yml
exec sesam config reset
! stdout .
stderr 'cannot be repaired in place'
exec sesam config reset --force
exists sesam.yml
exec sesam config diff
! stdout .

# The rewritten file has every user and secret the log knows.
grep 'name: admin' sesam.yml
grep 'name: bob' sesam.yml
grep 'README.md' sesam.yml

-- edited.yml --
users:
  - name: admin
    key:
      - $ADMIN_PUBKEY
  - name: bob
    key:
      - $BOB_PUBKEY
  - name: carol
    key:
      - $CAROL_PUBKEY

groups:
  admin:
    - admin
  dev:
    - bob
    - carol

secrets:
  - path: README.md
    access:
      - dev

-- broken.yml --
this is: [not
  valid yaml at all
